commands.check: Check the images of every view against its pixel density

lcp.lazy: The LCP image loads lazily (loading="lazy"), so it starts late. Load it eagerly with fetchpriority="high".
lcp.priority: The LCP image has no fetchpriority="high", so the browser may fetch it late.

findings.oversized: The file is {file} px, {ratio}× the {needed} px that {rendered} CSS px need at {dpr}x. Above {factor}×, the view loads more than it shows.

sizes-missing.img: The srcset gives widths (w) but the image has no sizes, so the browser takes the full viewport width and picks too large a file.
sizes-missing.source: A <source> of the picture gives widths (w) but no sizes, so the browser takes the full viewport width and picks too large a file.

findings.undersized: The file is {file} px, only {ratio}× the {needed} px that {rendered} CSS px need at {dpr}x. Below {factor}×, it looks blurred.

panel.cut: The answer was shortened to the images with problems; MCP images_check gives all of it.
panel.failed: This view could not be checked: {reason}
panel.hidden: {count, plural, one {# image} other {# images}} without problems left out.
panel.lcpGuessed: The page named no LCP element; the largest image of the first screen is taken for it.
panel.loading: Checking the images of every view…
panel.more: {count, plural, one {# more image is} other {# more images are}} not listed.
panel.noProblems: Every image fits this view's density.
panel.reported: {count, plural, one {# finding} other {# findings}} sent to the findings panel.
panel.summary: {error, plural, one {# error} other {# errors}}, {warning, plural, one {# warning} other {# warnings}}, {info, plural, one {# note} other {# notes}}

rules.lcp: The LCP image loads lazily or without high priority
rules.oversized: An image file far larger than the view's density needs
rules.sizes-missing: A srcset with widths and no sizes
rules.undersized: An image file smaller than the view's density needs

checkLcp.description: Check that the page's Largest Contentful Paint image loads eagerly and with fetchpriority="high".
checkLcp.help: The LCP image is the element the page reports as its Largest Contentful Paint; without one, the largest image of the first screen. When off, it leaves the loading and fetchpriority of that image unchecked.
checkLcp.label: Check the LCP image

oversizeFactor.description: An image file with more than this many times the pixels its rendered size needs at the view's density is too large (1.1 to 10).
oversizeFactor.help: Needed are the CSS pixels the image is drawn at times the view's device pixel ratio. Example: 1.5 flags a 1200 px wide file drawn 300 CSS px wide at 2x (600 px needed, 2 times as many).
oversizeFactor.label: Too large above

undersizeFactor.description: An image file with less than this many times the pixels its rendered size needs at the view's density is too small and looks blurred (0.1 to 1).
undersizeFactor.help: 1 flags every file with fewer pixels than the view shows (a pixel of rounding allowed); 0.75 accepts a file a quarter smaller.
undersizeFactor.label: Too small below

tools.check: The images of the target views, each measured at its view's device pixel ratio: the file the browser took from srcset or picture, its own pixels against the rendered size times the density, sizes, loading, fetchpriority and the LCP image, with the problems (too large, too small, srcset widths without sizes, LCP image lazy or without high priority). Reports nothing to the findings panel.
tools.mark: Marks an image (by its CSS selector) in the views named and scrolls it into view, or clears every mark.
